problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=\frac{4}{(t+1)^{3}}$, where $t\ge 0$ is the time. If the particle has position $x=1$ and velocity $v=-\frac{1}{2}$ when $t=1$, calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t>0.$

feedback.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with velocity $v(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t),$ where $t$ is the time. If the particle is at the position $x=3$ when $t=0,$ calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t>0.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We start by integrating the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $x(0)=3.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3 & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4(0))+C \\ 3 & =0+C \\ C & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is

$$
x(t)=3+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t).
$$
